summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS router) and node2 (OPNsense router) across their transit link (10.0.0.1/30 - 10.0.0.2/30; tunnel wg0 10.99.0.1/10.99.0.2), joining node1's private network A (10.10.1.0/24, host node3) with node2's private network B (10.10.2.0/24, host node4). node3 and node4 now reach each other by their private addresses, with tcpdump confirming only encrypted WireGuard UDP/51820 traffic crosses the transit link (no plaintext leakage). All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time (node3, node4, node2, node1), each verified via a changed OS-native boot identity (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) and full post-restart recovery of interfaces, the WireGuard tunnel, static routes, and node3<->node4 connectivity, with only one node down at a time throughout.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes' interfaces; discovered true L2 adjacency via arping (routed ping is misleading on this platform since a shared gateway proxies traffic between otherwise-isolated subnets)
Assigned transit addresses: node1 eth1=10.0.0.1/30, node2 vtnet1=10.0.0.2/30
Assigned private network A: node1 eth2=10.10.1.1/24, node3 eth1=10.10.1.2/24 (persisted in /etc/network/interfaces)
Assigned private network B: node2 vtnet2=10.10.2.1/24, node4 eth1=10.10.2.2/24 (persisted in /etc/network/interfaces)

Generated WireGuard keypairs on node1 (VyOS PKI) and node2 (wg genkey); configured wg0 on both with tunnel 10.99.0.0/30, port 51820, and correct peer public keys (fixed a stale pubkey after VyOS key regeneration)

On OPNsense node2: added opt1(transit)/opt2(privB)/opt3(wg0) interface assignments, WireGuard server+client model entries in config.xml, firewall pass rules for WG handshake/transit/privB/wg0, created missing /usr/local/etc/wireguard directory, reloaded interfaces/wireguard/filter
On VyOS node1: configured wg0 interface, peer, and static route to 10.10.2.0/24 via the tunnel; committed and saved
Added static routes on node3 (10.10.2.0/24 via 10.10.1.1) and node4 (10.10.1.0/24 via 10.10.2.1), persisted via /etc/network/interfaces 'up' hooks
Verified handshake, bidirectional ping node3<->node4, and via tcpdump on node1 eth1 that only encrypted UDP/51820 crosses the transit link
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, tunnel/route/service state) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node3 (Alpine reboot), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered eth1/route/ping to node4
Restarted node4 (Alpine reboot), confirmed changed boot_id and recovered eth1/route/ping to node3
Restarted node2 (OPNsense shutdown -r now), confirmed changed kern.boottime, and confirmed WireGuard/interfaces/pf rules and tunnel reconnected automatically from persisted config.xml
Restarted node1 (VyOS reboot), confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed wg0/peer/route recovered from persisted config.boot
Re-verified full node3<->node4 bidirectional connectivity after all four restarts

evidence.summary: arping-based L2 discovery confirmed node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 and node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 pairings; ifconfig showed node2's remaining interfaces to pair with node4

evidence.requirement: WireGuard tunnel established between node1 and node2
evidence.summary: wg show output on both sides shows matching public keys, endpoint, allowed-ips, and a fresh 'latest handshake' timestamp

evidence.requirement: Hosts reach each other by private addresses, traffic travels inside the tunnel
evidence.summary: bidirectional ping between node3 (10.10.1.2) and node4 (10.10.2.2) succeeds; tcpdump on node1's transit interface during the ping shows only encrypted UDP/51820 packets, proving the private traffic is tunneled and not sent in the clear
